Nikhilesh Dutta, Deputy Attorney-General with Md Abdul Baset, Assistant Attorney-General and Fara Mahmuda, Assistant Attorney-General — For the State. 

Abdul Malek with Sarwar Ahmed, AKM Shafiqul Islam and SM Shahjahan, Advocates — For the Condemned Prisoners.

State ------ Petitioner
Vs
Ershad Ali Sikder @ Ershad Sikder ------ Condemned Prisoner

3. Over the said occurrence, the informant had lodged a first information report on 30-3-90 at 2-15 AM against the condemned prisoners and six other accused persons. The Khulna Sadar police had registered a case being Khulna PS Case No.19 dated 30-9-90, which gave rise to GR Case No.150 of 1990. The Khulna police after investigation submitted a charge-sheet in the case against 12 accused persons and final report in favour of Ershad Sikder. The learned Magistrate accepted the police report, discharged Ershad Sikder and sent the case record to the learned Sessions Judge, Khulna where Sessions Case No. 103 of 1994 was registered. Accused persons including one Md Faruque Hossain and Md Nasiruddin Khan stood charged under sections 149/302/34 of the Penal Code. The accused persons who faced the charges pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. The learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court Khulna found all the accused persons not guilty of the charges and acquitted them by judgment and order dated 28-11-95. 

 6. Prosecution in support of its case has examined 16 witnesses and tendered 2 witnesses. Md Nur Alam (PW 1) has been examined as an accomplice. Md Osman Gani @ Babu (PW 2) is the informant. Sahinur Begum (PW 3) is the mother of the victim. Most Bokul Begum (PW 4) is not an eyewitness of the occurrence who claims that she has heard from PW 2. Md Jamaluddin (PW 5) is a chance witness and an eyewitness of the occurrence. He is the brother-in-law of the deceased Nantu. Md Selim Hossain (PW 6) claims that he is an eyewitness of the occurrence. He has admitted enmity with the accused persons. Doctor Md Moazzam Hossain (PW 7) recorded the dying declaration of the deceased Nantu and proved his signature in the dying declaration. Md Halim Molla (PW 9) is a formal witness. He has been declared hostile. Abdul Khaleque Howlader (PW 10) is a constable who has carried the dead body to the morgue. Md Sabir Ahmed (PW 11) is a Magistrate, who recorded the confessional statement of Md Nur Alam (PW 1) in Khulna PS Case No. 23 dated 19-5-99. Chandra Bhoson Majumder (PW 12) is a police officer who prays for further investigation into the case after acquittal of the accused persons in Sessions Case No. 103 of 1994. Doctor MA Gafur (PW 14) and Doctor Md Amanullah (PW 15) are witnesses of the dying declaration. Md AKM Shahjahan Ali (PW 16) has partly investigated the case. Abdul Matin Bhuiyan (PW 17) has completed the investigation of the case. Doctor Akram Ali (PW 18) performs the autopsy on the dead body of the deceased. 

 7. Mr MA Malek, learned Counsel appearing for the condemned prisoners, has raised a preliminary point about the legality and the jurisdiction for holding the trial of the condemned prisoners in the case. He submits that the condemned prisoners Faruque Faruque Khan © Jamai Faruque and Nasir Khan have been acquitted of the charge of murder on a full-fledged trial over the self-same occurrence in Sessions Case No.103 of 1994 and their trial for the second time is barred under section 403 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He further submitted that Ershad Sikder was discharged by an order dated 14-10-90 of the learned Magistrate in pursuance of submission of final report in his favour, against which order of discharge, the State did not take any exception. According to him, this order of discharge tantamounts to an order of acquittal for all practical purposes. He cannot be vexed again for the same occurrence. In support of his contention he has referred the case of Abul Hossain Sana vs Sunwalal Agarwala and another 14 DLR (SC) 96. 

 8. On perusal of the order sheet and the evidence on record, we have noticed that an intricate law point is involved in this case. Accordingly, by order dated 3-3-2004, we requested the learned Additional Attorney-General (Criminal) to assist this court to meet the points involved in this case. We have communicated the order through Mr Mohammed Abdul Baset, learned Assistant Attorney-General. The learned Deputy Attorney-General and the learned Assistant Attorney-General intimate this Court that they HC-38 have communicated the order of this Court and that the learned Additional Attorney-General will address this Court. When the matter is taken up for hearing, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that the learned Additional Attorney-General will be able to address this court. No adjournment has been sought for on his behalf and therefore, we are expecting that he will be able to address this Court but to our utter surprise, the learned Additional Attorney-General has not turned up. We fail to understand why the learned Additional Attorney-General has undermined the authority of this Court. If the Additional Attorney-General disregards an order of this Court, what else can be expected from the other junior law officers of the State. We express our concern about the conduct of the leaned Additional Attorney-General. 

 10. PW 2 in clear terms states "দায়রা ১০৩/৯৮ নং মামলায় সাক্ষ্য দেওয়া কালে বলেছিলেন যে, ২৯-৩-৯০ তারিখে সদ্যা ৭-৪৫/৮-০০ টার মধ্যে আমি বাসায় ছিলাম ৷তখন কয়েকজন লোক এসে বলে আমার ভাই নান্টুকে খেলার মাঠে নিয়ে গেছে ৷ উক্ত খবর গুনে রেলওয়ে মাঠে যাই ৷ সেখানে কাউকে দেখতে ই নাই ৷ তার পরে আমি খুলনা সদর হাসপাতালে যাই এবং আমার ভাইয়ের চিকিৎসা চলছিল ৷ চিকিৎসা চলাকালে দারোগা সাহেব হসপিটালে আসে এবং দারোগা সাহেব একটা কাগজে সহি করতে বলে এবং আমি উক্ত কাগজে সহি করি ৷ কেস করার ব্যাপারে কাগজে সহি করি ৷ আমার ভাই দুইদিন পর হাসপাতালে মারা যায় ৷ কিছুদিন পর আমাকে দারোগা সাহেব কোর্টে নিয়ে আসে ৷ কোর্টে ম্যাজিস্ট্রেট সাহেবের সামনে বসে রেখে কিছু কাগজে আমার সহি নেয় ৷ কিছুদিন পর আমাকে ডি বি অফিসে নিয়ে গিয়ে সাদা কাগজে সহি নেয় ৷ আমার ভাই হাসপাতালে মারা যায় ৷ আমার ভাইকে কে হত্যা করেছে আমি দেখি নাই ৷ ইহা সত্য নয় যে, আসামী ফারুক রামদা দিয়া আমার ভাইয়ের মাথায় কোপ দেয় একথা সম্পূর্ন জোর করে আমাকে বলানো হয়েছে ৷ ইহা সত্য নয় যে, অন্যান্য আসামীরা তাদের হাতে থাকা অস্ত্র দ্বারা আমার ভইিকে মারপিট করে একথা ও জোর করে আমাকে দিয়া বলানো হয়েছে ৷ আমি দায়রা ১০৩/৯৪  মোকদ্দমায় আমি সাক্ষ্য দিয়া যা বলেছি সবই সঠিক বলে ছিলাম ইহা সত্য নয় ৷ আমাকে হুমকি দিয়া উক্ত মামলায় উক্তরূপ সাক্ষ্য দেওয়ানো হয়েছে ৷ হুমকি দেওয়ার কথাও পূর্বের পি, পি, সাহেবকে বলি নাই ৷ বললে তো আমাকে মেরে ফেলবে ৷ উক্ত সময় উক্তরূপ হুমকির বিষয়ে কোন জজকে বলি নাই ৷" His admissions as above are relevant under section 21 of the Evidence Act, inasmuch as, when a statement is made in the "self harming" form, it is receivable and is usually considered proof of a very satisfactory kind. Such statements are admissible and original evidence as part of the resgestae when made at the time the state of mind or body existed, whether they be in favour or against the prosecution. 

 11. PW 3, the mother of the deceased, is not an eyewitness. She "জনৈক ব্যক্তি এসে বলে এরশাদ সিকদার ও তার লোকেরা নান্টুকে ধরে নিয়ে গেছে " PW 4 states that she has heard from PW 2 about the incident. We have discarded the evidence of PW 2 earlier and therefore, no reliance can be given to her testimony. PWs 5 and 6 claim as eyewitnesses. PW 5 is the cousin of the deceased. He has deposed in the earlier trial and the Court discarded his testimony. PW 6 also deposed as witness in the earlier trial. His testimony was also discarded. He has admitted enmity with the accused. PW 7 recorded the dying declaration of the deceased and he has also been examined and his evidence has been discarded by earlier trial Court. PWs 14 and 15 have not been examined in the earlier trial. Now they have been examined to corroborate the testimony of PW 7. We cannot re-assess the testimony of all these witnesses again unless the earlier judgment is set aside. The witnesses who are vacillating in their testimony cannot be relied upon. The learned Additional Sessions Judge has ignored this aspect of the matter and believed these witnesses as if he is trying the case afresh. 

 13. Sub-section (3B) of section 173 of the Code of Criminal Procedure empowers the officer-in-charge of the police station to hold further investigation in respect of an offence after a report under sub-section (1) of section 173 has been forwarded to the Magistrate, and where upon such investigation, the police officer obtains further evidence, he shall forward to the Magistrate a further report regarding such evidence in the manner as provided under sub-section (1). This provision has been inserted by Ordinance No. XLIX of 1978 and by this provision, the police officer has been given unlimited power to submit a supplementary police report if further oral or documentary evidence is collected at any stage of the proceeding, even after taking cognisance of the offence. The police officer has full freedom without the intervention of the Magistrate to submit a supplementary charge-sheet or further report, as the case may be, before the conclusion of trial of the case. But this does not mean that he can exercise such power even after the conclusion of the trial of the case. He cannot re-open a case for investigation after the trial of the case. If this process is allowed, there will be no end to any litigation and any proceeding can be re-opened at the sweet will of the police officer, which is not the intention of the legislature for inserting this provision. Similarly, no Magistrate has any power to accord permission to re-open a case at his whim. He cannot sit over the matter after the trial of the case. An accused person may not be vexed on repeated occasions on this or that reason, so long the order of discharge or acquittal stands and so long the said order has not been set aside by a superior Court. The learned Deputy Attorney-General is unable to meet this point. The learned Deputy Attorney-General fails to cite any authority in support of the prosecution case that a second trial of the accused persons or by adding any other accused on the self same charge is permissible. He however, submits that the condemned prisoners are veteran criminals and if, on technical ground, they are acquitted, the prosecution will be highly prejudiced. 

 14. A further investigation of a case may be conducted by the investigating agency where fresh facts come to light. There is no express provision prohibiting the police from launching upon an investigation into the fresh facts coming to light after submission of the report under section 173(1) CrPC even after the Magistrate has taken cognisance of the offence. It is in the interests of both the prosecution and the defence that the police should have such power. It is easy to visualise a case where fresh material may come to light which will implicate persons not previously accused or absolve persons already accused where the involvement of persons who are not already accused comes to the notice of the investigating agency, it cannot keep quiet and refuse to investigate the fresh information. But this is not such a case in which a further investigation may be conducted on the simple ground that the proceeding has been terminated on a full-fledged trial and the Code does not permit such course of action. No fresh material came to light after such investigation. It has been stated in the supplementary charge-sheet that the statement of Nur Alam under section 164 CrPC and the dying declaration of Nantu have proved the complicity of the accused persons and that Nasir and Faruque are not the persons who have been charge-sheeted earlier. We have discarded the testimony of Nur Alam earlier on the ground that he has not made any statement under section 164 CrPC. As regards the statement that Nasir and Faruque have not been charge sheeted in the earlier police report, PW 17 makes similar statement in his testimony. According to him, they have not been tried in the earlier case.  This is totally a false statement, which will be evident from the testimony of PW 2 who identified Nasir, Faruque and Ershad in the dock as accused persons against whom he lodged first information report on 30-3-90. This statement proved that they were first information report-named accused persons. In the first information report in the column of the accused persons, Faruque is at serial No. 2 and Chhoto Nasir is serial No. 3. The original charge-sheet shows that the investigating officer has submitted charge-sheet against all other first information report-named accused persons except Ershad Sikder. The learned Magistrate has accepted the said police report and after compliance of formalities, the case record has been sent for trial, which has given rise to Sessions Case No. 103 of 1994. Accused Nasir and Faruque, in reply to their examination under section 342 CrPC, state that they have been acquitted in Sessions Case No. 103 of 1994. This positive statements of these condemned prisoners coupled with the statement of PW 2 proved that Nasir and Faruque had faced trial in sessions case No.103 of 1994 and that they were acquitted of the charge. The original police report was a complete one and there was no inherent lacuna in it and that the accused persons were acquitted on a full-fledged trial. The learned Magistrate in the premises was not justified in permitting further investigation of the case. The learned Additional Sessions Judge has not considered this point despite the fact that they have raised the legality of their trial over the self-same occurrence. 

 "The argument that section 403 does not create a bar cannot be conclusive in the face of the well-established principle that there is to be an end to litigation and that as a general rule a person is not to be vexed twice in respect of the same matter. As has already been observed if full effect was given to the argument that where a bar is not created by section 403 CrPC the bar does not exist at all, there will be no end to successive proceedings which, on exactly the same evidence, may be taken before a Magistrate against a particular accused person............ As long as there is no provision for a review proceedings once taken on the merits cannot be reopened. Of course, the revisional Court has full powers in all cases where any sufficient reasons exist to direct fresh inquiry for the bar itself is based on a general principle and is not regulated by any technical consideration." 

 19. Before parting with, we would like to make some observations about the conduct of the prosecuting agency and the learned Additional Sessions Judge. PW 16 Md AKM Shahjahan, Mr Ruhul Amin, the then Assistant Superintendent of Police and Mr Khandakar Yakub Ali of Detective Branch investigated the case and came to the conclusion that Ershad Sikder was not present at the time of the occurrence. In the first information report he was the accused serial No.1. In the dying declaration recorded by PW 7, the declarant disclosed the name of Ershad as accused No.1 and still then, the investigating agencies did not find his complicity was mysterious. The learned Magistrate accepted the report and discharged him in a laconic order as if he were performing a routine work. The prosecution did not challenge the order of discharge and proceeded with the trial without the principal accused. The prosecution did not take any step for examination of PWs 14 and 15 in whose presence the dying declaration was recorded. The learned Additional Sessions Judge disbelieved the dying declaration mainly on the ground that the prosecution ought to have examined those two doctors for proving that the declarant's condition was not so serious to make such a declaration. This led us to believe - that the prosecuting agency with a view to screen the real offender from legal punishment caused the legal evidence to disappear and thereafter staged a drama for his trial after reviving the case as an eyewash. Similarly, Mr Taj Mohammad Sheikh, the learned Additional Sessions Judge also failed to adorn himself above them by allowing the prosecuting agency to successfully stage the drama of trial of the condemned prisoners. This has incurred in us pangs and agony on the mode of administration of criminal justice in respect of offences punishable by death. We are of the view that the administration of criminal justice is not safe in his hands. The learned Additional Sessions Judge has exceeded the norms as a judge in wasting his valuable time at the cost of the public exchequer.
